description: Align the cam-worker container user uid/gid to the host user at build time so container workers can WRITE the bind-mounted /workspace (fixes the EACCES that blocks all container workers, CAM-175 finding).

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed: an ARG comes into effect only from the line it is declared, so ARG HOST_UID/HOST_GID must precede the RUN that uses them and sit before USER bun. ARG NAME=default supplies a fallback when no --build-arg is passed. --build-arg for an ARG NOT declared in the Dockerfile is accepted without error (silent no-op), so host-mode builds that omit the flag are safe.

userStories.title: Re-home the bun user to HOST_UID/HOST_GID build-args in the worker image
userStories.description: As the cam maintainer, I need the cam-worker Docker image to re-home the bun user to a caller-provided uid/gid at build time, and the docker-build argv builder to emit those as --build-arg, so a container worker's process uid matches the host owner of the bind-mounted /workspace and can write it instead of hitting EACCES.
acceptanceCriteria: .devcontainer/Dockerfile declares ARG HOST_UID and ARG HOST_GID (default 1000) before the RUN that consumes them, and re-homes the bun user (usermod -u $HOST_UID bun + groupmod -g $HOST_GID bun) BEFORE the USER bun directive. [oracle: grep -Eq 'ARG HOST_UID' .devcontainer/Dockerfile && grep -Eq 'ARG HOST_GID' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The Dockerfile runs chown -R $HOST_UID:$HOST_GID /home/bun after the usermod/groupmod (usermod -u does not re-own existing files, so the chown is required). [oracle: grep -q 'chown -R' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The groupmod step handles a pre-existing group already owning the target gid (e.g. macOS staff gid 20) without aborting the build (guarded via getent group $HOST_GID or equivalent). [oracle: grep -q 'getent group' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

buildDockerBuildArgv accepts hostUid and hostGid options and emits --build-arg HOST_UID=<uid> and --build-arg HOST_GID=<gid> when both are provided. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/worker-container.test.ts]

When hostUid/hostGid are absent, buildDockerBuildArgv emits NO --build-arg token: the default argv is byte-identical to today so host mode is unaffected. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/worker-container.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
userStories.notes: Files: .devcontainer/Dockerfile, src/supervisor/worker-container.ts (DockerBuildArgvOptions + buildDockerBuildArgv), test/supervisor/worker-container.test.ts. Read scripts/cam/patterns.md first. Place the ARG/usermod/groupmod/chown block BEFORE the existing `USER bun` directive (currently line ~46); ARG must be declared before the RUN that references it (Docker: an ARG comes into effect from its declaration line, confirmed in officialDocsConsulted). gid-collision gotcha: `groupmod -g` fails if another group already owns that gid (macOS staff gid 20 is the common collision); guard with `getent group $HOST_GID` and only groupmod when the gid is free (or rename the colliding group). Keep `--user bun` in buildDockerRunArgv unchanged: the re-homed bun user now carries the host uid. Do NOT add a Write tool as a workaround (gotcha: the root cause is the uid mismatch, not a missing tool). CI has NO Docker: assert the argv wiring via the pure buildDockerBuildArgv builder, never a live build. worker-container-parity.test.ts reads devcontainer.json for run-arg parity; the build-arg is a build-time concern and is not declared in devcontainer.json, so parity is unaffected.

userStories.title: Resolve host uid/gid and thread build-args through the production ensure-up path
userStories.description: As the sidecar, I need the container ensure-up path to resolve the host user's uid/gid (id -u / id -g) and pass them as build-args so a rebuild produces a uid-aligned image, while host mode stays byte-identical (never invoked, no build-args emitted).
acceptanceCriteria: A resolveHostIds helper (injectable spawn seam) returns { uid, gid } parsed from `id -u` / `id -g`, falling back to { uid: 1000, gid: 1000 } when the command fails or returns a non-numeric value. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/worker-container.test.ts]

makeProductionEnsureContainerFn resolves the host uid/gid via resolveHostIds and forwards them as build.hostUid / build.hostGid into ensureWorkerContainer. [oracle: grep -q 'resolveHostIds' src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts]

The resolved build.hostUid / build.hostGid reach the docker build argv on BOTH the absent (created) and image-stale (rebuilt) branches of ensureWorkerContainer. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts]

Host mode is unchanged: when worker_isolation is absent/host the ensure-up path is never invoked (zero docker calls) and no --build-arg is emitted. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts]

The claude-code-config named-volume upgrade caveat (a stale uid-1000 volume keeps old ownership; a one-time `docker volume rm claude-code-config` is required on upgrade so the re-homed user owns /home/bun/.claude) is documented in docs/recovery-runbook.md. [oracle: grep -q 'docker volume rm claude-code-config' docs/recovery-runbook.md]
Quality spine green (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/worker-container.ts (add exported resolveHostIds with a ContainerSpawnFn-style injectable seam), src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts (makeProductionEnsureContainerFn sets build: { hostUid, hostGid }), test/supervisor/worker-container.test.ts, test/supervisor/ensure-container.test.ts, docs/recovery-runbook.md. Depends on US-001 (the hostUid/hostGid fields on DockerBuildArgvOptions). ensureWorkerContainer ALREADY forwards `build: opts.build` to runWorkerContainer on both the created and rebuilt branches (ensure-container.ts:146,163), so the factory only needs to populate build. resolveHostIds: wrap spawnSync('id',['-u']) / ('id',['-g']) with encoding utf8; Number.parseInt(trimmed, 10); guard Number.isNaN -> 1000 (noUncheckedIndexedAccess: handle undefined/empty stdout). Image-stale rebuild trigger fires on Dockerfile mtime bump; the US-001 Dockerfile edit bumps mtime so the first landing rebuilds correctly (the build-arg-only-change case is out of scope here). Live behavioral confirmation (docker exec cam-worker touch /workspace) is the downstream CAM-175 re-run ceremony run by the operator OUTSIDE the autonomous loop (CI has no Docker; also gated on CAM-179 onboarding/trust seed); it is intentionally not an in-loop story. OUT OF SCOPE: the onboarding/trust seed (CAM-179), firewall wiring (CAM-176), and any dispatch change beyond the container build/run args.
